title: Open-source tool designs LEGO builds with more than 2,000 real pieces — their programs output detailed CAD files, but no models have been built yet
key_facts: Open-source tool LDraw Nova lets AI models design LEGO builds from a prompt, producing LDraw CAD files.
One example is the 2,175-piece Sakura Garden, from a prompt to Claude Opus 5.5.
Developer Carlos Antelo posted it on Friday after three earlier attempts.
No design has been built with real bricks; Antelo says he 'didn't even try'.
Limits: no physics or stability checking, and only frontier models make large accurate builds.
Antelo's 'wild' estimate is about $5 in token costs for Astra building one Technic mechanism.
It differs from Carnegie Mellon's LegoGPT/BrickGPT, which checks stability.
quote_evidence: None of the designs have been built with real bricks yet, though; developer Carlos Antelo says he "didn't even try."
"physics modeling is something Nova is currently lacking"
why_it_matters_hint: AI agents can now plan large LEGO models as files, but nothing has been tested in real bricks.
notes: Released Friday 2 Oct, before the window; score lowered by 1.
